explanations.text:
This file is the front desk of the human tool. It does not do the
work itself: it reads what you typed and passes it to the hand
that does it. Here is what each thing you can type becomes.

[human init](cmd_init):
  creates the human folder in the project.
  the reader page
  human/human.json with the list of the project's files.
    
  if none yet, human/human.json gets a short random name as an id
  prints the id and the count of files.
  training store keeps the sessions of the project under it.
    
  [sweep](scan_files) the project folder and its code files
  drop hidden files, 
  build folders, 
  if folders with a map of their own then pass through [the sieve](is_ignored)
  fill the ignore list of human.json
  add human files to human.json, each with the folder it shows in
  
  if it doesn't exist yet, create human/project.json, the map of the whole project. 
  if a file at the top of the folder answers to the word "project", or to the bare name of a human file:
    show warning that the file needs a new path to be told apart.

[human serve](cmd_serve):
    finds the top of the project and opens a door for the
    browser, 8010 unless you say --port. 
    prints the localhost address, the [tailnet address](tailnet_ip) when the machine
    is on one, the line that says an open training session
    shows as a layer over the reader, the line that says a new
    file from the reader lands empty next to the others, and
    the line that says where a writing from the
    reader lands. 
    behind the door stands [the fresh copy](FreshHandler). it can serve:
      a file of the project handed out as it is on disk
      /human/human.json, [rebuilt](fresh_map) on every request, so a new file, and a new human file show on reload.
      /human/training/, which is the list of this project's training sessions, kept in the training store away from this machine.
      /human/training/<name>.json, one of the training sessions, by its name; a session of another project gets "not found".
      /human/server/queue, the updates that are not worked yet by the ai harness.
    
    and takes five kinds of writing, [the body](read_body) read as JSON:

      a pick from the training layer        ([the pick](do_POST)) — the row, the
                                              version and your reason go into the
                                              session file
      a close from the training layer       — the session closes as with
                                              human train --close: each picked row
                                              goes into its map. A close for a
                                              session that is not the open one is
                                              refused
      a writing from the reader             — your own words on an entry, a first
                                              telling for a file with no map, or the
                                              code of that file; the desk hands it to
                                              [the queue](compiler/cli/human/cmd_watch.py:compile_writing),
                                              which runs the command you would have
                                              typed and keeps the writing for claude.
                                              When the writing grows a few words of an
                                              entry, the desk passes those marked words
                                              along with it, so the queue knows which
                                              part to grow
      a new file from the reader            ([the new file](new_file)) — you name a
                                              path from the top of the project; the
                                              desk makes the file there, empty, and
                                              puts it in the list of the book, so it
                                              waits for its telling. A path that leaves
                                              the project, goes into the human folder,
                                              a hidden or build folder, or a project of
                                              its own, a name with a dot in front, a
                                              suffix the list does not know, a path the
                                              ignore list drops, or a file that is
                                              already there is refused, with the reason

       if a new human file from the reader:
         one bare word, no folder and no suffix,
         [the folder](human_place) you made it in, which the map keeps as its place; 
         the desk opens an empty map under that name, for words that stand on no code. 
         a name with a folder, a suffix or a dot in front, 
         the word "project", a name another human file holds, or a name a file at the root holds is refused, with the reason. 
         a folder is dropped if it leaves the project to go to:
           the human folder, 
           a hidden or build folder, 
           or not on disk
         the map stands at the top

    Any other writing gets "not found". An ask for training when
    the machine has no key, when the book has no id, or when the
    store does not answer, gets the reason back in place of the
    sessions. Every answer
    carries "do not keep me" ([the note](end_headers)), so a
    reload never shows an old copy, and the desk stays quiet
    unless you add --log ([the mute](log_message)).

[human map file --verbatim](compiler/cli/human/cmd_map.py)
  an abstraction the user sends.
  if --verbatim yes, mark as verbatim.
  the name is a file, the word "project", or a human file by its bare name.
  the desk hands the whole line to the map run
  [the guard](compiler/cli/human/cmd_map.py) there keeps the words as you wrote them — they go in plain. 
  a pin in the abstraction is refused.

human retext, undo, show, lines, sync <file>       ([the engine](compiler/cli/human/decompiler.py))
    All the work on a map that exists. The desk only points
    the way. retext takes --verbatim too, to put words of your
    own in the place of the ones already mapped. undo takes
    --entry, the number of the entry to drop; without it the
    last entry written goes.

human retext, undo, show, lines, sync project      ([the project hand](compiler/cli/human/cmd_project.py))
    The same commands with the word "project" where the file
    goes: the desk sends them to the hand that works on the
    map of the whole project, before the engine sees them.

human train --open / file --as best --shape sections / --close
                                                  ([the trainer](compiler/cli/human/cmd_train.py))
    Three versions of one abstraction, each with the name of
    the shape it follows; a pick in the feed; the pick mapped
    at the close.
    With --target and --words the versions grow the marked
    words of that entry: at the close the new entry is mapped,
    and the pin of the target into it waits for claude.

human watch / human ack <number>                   ([the watch](compiler/cli/human/cmd_watch.py))
    The other side of a writing from the reader. watch prints
    every writing claude has not finished, one line each, and
    stays at the queue for the next; --once prints and returns.
    ack marks the writing with that number as done and says
    how many still wait.

human login <key>                                  ([the store hand](compiler/cli/human/cmd_store.py))
    Gives this machine the key to the training store. The desk
    hands the key on; the store says who the key belongs to and
    the key is kept in your home folder, so every later ask for
    a training session carries it.

human skills                                        ([the giver](cmd_skills))
    Copies the skill folders, shapes included, to where your
    agent looks for them.

The one line that ties it together is [the front door](main):
it names every command above, says which flags each one takes —
for map and retext: --verbatim; for undo: --entry; for train:
--open, --close, --as, --shape, --kind, --entry, --block, --target,
--words, --text;
for watch: --once, for ack the number of the writing, and for
login the key — and hands the parsed line to the right hand.

explanations.text:
●  you open the door                                    ([the shelf](cmd_serve))
  │     You type: human serve.
  │     The tool climbs to the top of the project — the folder
  │     that holds human/ — so the command works from any
  │     folder inside the project.
  │     Then it takes door 8010 of your machine and stands there.
  │     It prints the addresses to read at, the line that tells
  │     you an open training session shows as a layer over the
  │     reader, the line that tells you a new file from the
  │     reader lands empty next to the others, the line that
  │     tells you a new human file takes a bare name and opens
  │     with no file under it, and the line that tells you a
  │     writing in the reader lands in human/server/.
  │
  ●  the browser knocks                             ([the fresh copy](FreshHandler))
  │     You open http://localhost:8010/human/web.html.
  │     Each thing on the page — the reader, the maps, the code —
  │     is one knock: "give me this file".
  │     The tool hands out only files under the top of the
  │     project, never anything above it.
  │
  ●  the feed sends a pick back                          ([the pick](do_POST))
  │     The training layer over the reader shows you two texts
  │     and you choose one. The choice comes back as one knock
  │     of its own, and the tool writes it into the training
  │     session.
  │     When you close the session from the layer, that is one
  │     knock too: the tool closes it as human train --close
  │     does, and each picked row goes into its map. A close for
  │     a session that is not the open one is refused.
  │
  ●  the reader sends a writing back
  │     In the reader you can write yourself: new words for an
  │     entry, a first telling for a file with no map, or the
  │     code of that file. The writing comes back as its own
  │     knock and the tool puts it in the queue in human/server/,
  │     where the agent takes it with human watch. When you mark
  │     a few words of an entry to grow them, those words go with
  │     the writing, so the agent knows which part to grow.
  │     The page can also ask for that queue and see what still
  │     waits.
  │
  ●  the reader asks for a new file                  ([the new file](new_file))
  │     In the reader you can name a path from the top of the
  │     project. The tool makes the file there, empty, and puts
  │     it in the list of files in human/human.json, so it waits
  │     for its telling. It refuses, with the reason, a path that
  │     leaves the project, goes into the human folder, a hidden
  │     or build folder, or a project of its own, a name with a
  │     dot in front, a suffix the file tree does not know, a
  │     path the ignore list drops, or a file that is already
  │     there.
  │
  ●  the reader asks for a new human file            ([the human file](new_human))
  │     In the reader you can also ask for words that stand on
  │     no code. You give one bare word — no folder, no suffix —
  │     and the tool opens an empty map under that name, ready
  │     for its abstraction, with no file under it. It refuses,
  │     with the reason, a name that carries a folder, a suffix
  │     or a dot in front, the word "project", a name another
  │     human file already holds, or a name a file at the root
  │     holds.
  │     With the name you can send [a folder](human_place) of the
  │     project to keep the map beside. The tool writes that
  │     folder into the map, so the reader shows the map there
  │     and the word back names it as that folder over the name.
  │     A folder that leaves the project, one in the human folder
  │     or in a hidden or build folder, and one that is not on
  │     disk, is dropped: the map stands at the top instead.
  │     A knock that is not a pick, a close, a writing, a new
  │     file, or a new human file gets "not found".
  │
  ●  every answer says: do not keep me                    ([the note](end_headers))
  │     The tool marks each file it hands out, so the browser
  │     asks fresh next time instead of showing an old copy.
  │     This is why a changed map shows up on a plain reload.
  │
  ●  the tool stands at the door until you stop it
        Ask after ask, it answers. Ctrl-c closes the door.
        Only a pick, a close, a writing, a new file, or a new human file changes the project; every
        other knock reads and leaves it as it is.

──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  when the answer is not a file                         ([the answer](send_json))
     The fresh map, the list of training sessions, the queue
     of waiting writings, and the word back from a pick, a close, a
     writing, a new file, or a new human file are not files on disk. The tool writes them out
     as one block of JSON with its length in front.

  when the page asks for training                      ([the reading](do_GET))
     The list of sessions, and one session by its name, do not
     live on this machine: the tool asks the training store for
     them and hands the answer on. The list holds only the
     sessions of this project, found by the id in
     human/human.json, and a session of another project gets
     "not found". When this machine has no key, the book has no
     id, or the store does not answer, the page gets the reason in
     place of the sessions.

  when you want to see the asks                           ([the mute](log_message))
     human serve --log writes one line per knock.
     Without it the tool stays silent, because one page load
     is many knocks and they would flood your screen.

  when a second project wants a door
     A machine gives each numbered door to one program only,
     and the first serve holds door 8010. Give the second
     project its own door: human serve --port 8011, and read
     it at http://localhost:8011/human/web.html.
